why: A group of year-round theme parks weighing plans costing up to EUR 50m upfront, with a few thousand extra visitors a day at EUR 9 to 14 profit each, is believable.

Truing the road range's 412 faulty wheels costs $52,900, about $128 or nearly 5 mechanic-hours at $27 per wheel, more than five times the $9,700 paid for all the road range's wheels; truing a wheel takes well under an hour, and at any real wheel price the faulty wheels would outnumber the wheels bought.
A medicines wholesaler handling about 2.4 million order lines a month, with a robot-picking funnel that narrows from 100% to 55-66%, is believable.
Almonds at $6 to $10 per kg, 0.1 kg per bag and 2.2 million bags a year (220 tonnes of almonds) fit a supermarket granola maker.

Members are placed in quintiles by how often they ride, yet Quintile 3 averages fewer rides than Quintile 2 in both years (34 vs 37 in 2011, 18 vs 30 in 2012), which cannot happen when the quintiles are ranked by ride frequency.
A cosmetics group with 172 products earning GBP 25m profit, about GBP 145,000 per product, is believable.
Booking growth split by trip type into app and website contributions of 0.1 to 0.7 percentage points, with each bar's parts adding to the stated totals, is believable.
Market sales of $9 to $25 billion per platform, with mobile growing quickly, are believable for a national or regional video game market.
A city bike-hire scheme with 64,000 members making 2.1 million trips and costing GBP 6.2m a year, about GBP 40 to 390 per member by group, is believable.
A mid-priced hotel group with revenues in the tens to hundreds of millions per line and margins of 7-15% is believable.
